Meſcou. The Revenues of the Patriarch, as alſo of the Metropolitans, 
are very great , out of which they are obliged to levy and Maintain 
an Army of 15000 men, during the time of War. 

The Habit of the Patriarch, and the Metropolitans differ but litle. 
The Patriarch has always a great Croſier born before him, or a litle 
one in his hand and ſometimes both , this they call a Pofok. Mitres 
they wear only upon Convocations or high Aiſemblies , and upon 
ſolemn Occaſions. Abroad they are diſtinguiſhed by a high Cap, 
fat at top like the Switzers, or Yeomen of the Guard. Next their 
Bodiethey wear a Caſloc, and above that a long Gown or rather a 
Pall, which is born up by two Gentlemen. The Inferior Clergy and 
Prieſts wear a Cap but not ſo high as that of the Supertors. This Cap is 
given them when they are ordained by the Biſhops , at what time 
they ſhave their Heads, and ſuffer it to grow no more, ſave in two litle 
tufts juſt above their cars. 

There is a Law among them that whoſoever beats one of thoſe 
Clerks ſo,that his cap fall to the ground,he is liable toa very ſevere pe- 
nalty ( if I well remember to looſe his hand ) which nevertheleſs

the Cap upon the right Block again.

The Nagayans follow the Fiſhing-trade, as alſo Fowling , Hunting 
and Paſturing of Cattel, and are reputed the beſt Herds-men in the 
world. Their Kine are generally great , their Sheep very fair and

200r 30 pound a piece , their noſes bending upwards , and their

very durable in running. They have alſo ſome Camels but not many, 
Their chief Diet is dried Fiſh which they uſe in ſtead of Bread. They 
have alſo a way of making bread of Rice, which they knead in Oil and 
Honey , and ſo bake it in Cakes. All kinds of Fleſh they eat , ex- 
cept Swine, holding Horſe-fleſh for the beſt. Their Drink is Water 
and Milk, efteeming Mares-milk aboveall other. They profeſs the 
Mahometan Religion , and are of the Perſian ſet. The Czar allows 
them Laws and Judges of their own. They are alſo Tribute-free , but
